characterList.description: A bearded man with dark hair and a black shirt. He is speaking directly to the camera in a room with a starry background.
characterList.name: Samir Dhurde

content_metadata.description: Analysis of a video featuring Samir Dhurde discussing the Moon Challenge.

qAndA.answer: Samir suggests using binoculars, a telescope, or a camera to observe the moon. He shows examples of sketches made by Galileo using a telescope and a series of photos forming a moon calendar.
qAndA.question: What type of observation equipment does Samir suggest using for the Moon Challenge?

qAndA.answer: Samir mentions being bored while staying at home and wanting to do something related to nature. He also highlights the disconnect people have with the natural world and how the challenge can help bridge that gap.
qAndA.question: What reason does Samir give for starting the Moon Challenge?

qAndA.answer: Samir plans to record the time of observation, the direction of the moon in the sky, its distance from the horizon, and its rising and setting times.
qAndA.question: What specific details does Samir plan to record about the moon during the challenge?

qAndA.answer: Samir mentions that the new moon is special because it is not visible, making it intriguing to discuss. He promises to delve deeper into this in the next video.
qAndA.question: Why is the new moon special according to Samir?

qAndA.answer: The visual of the globe lined up 30 times to reach the moon emphasizes the vast distance between Earth and the moon, adding to the sense of wonder and fascination surrounding space and astronomy.
qAndA.question: How does the visual of the globe add to the narrative?

narrativeProgression.description: Samir introduces himself, greets viewers, and discusses the context of the challenge.
Samir shares his personal experience of boredom while staying at home and proposes the Moon Challenge as a solution.
Samir highlights the simplicity of the challenge and its connection to nature. He talks about the cultural significance of the moon and its various names.
Samir encourages viewers to connect with nature by observing the moon and its movements. He emphasizes the knowledge gap in modern society regarding basic astronomical events.
Samir presents various activities for the Moon Challenge, including sketching, photography, and creating a moon calendar. He shows examples of each.

Samir concludes by encouraging viewers to stay tuned for updates on their YouTube channel and to subscribe for daily details. He also promises to discuss the specialty of the new moon in the next video.

Just look at the moon every day.
A few of us are promising to do this every day and also in turn to find out a lot of other
interesting facts about the moon and astronomy.
It will be of course great fun if you could join in.
What's better is that you can do this from the safety of your home.
A big hello to everybody from across the world.
I am Samir Dherde from Pune India.
I work at the Interunia City Centre for Astronomy and Astrophysics and I'm joined by my team
of the Outreach Group and a lot of astronomy lovers in this particular challenge.
Of course today we are facing a bigger challenge, a bigger crisis in which we are all playing
our little roles by staying at home.
We are doing this to avoid disaster.
Frankly speaking, I am bored of my mind by staying home.
Yes, that's a reality and I'm sure you are getting bored as well.
So we thought let us take a challenge.
It's a very simple challenge and it involves nature all along us.
Let us this month spend a little bit of time taking a step back and observing nature.
As an astronomer, I love looking at the sky and therefore I thought maybe we could take
up the challenge of looking at the moon for a month.
It's not a big amount of time or a big amount of investment that you are making here.
So all that we ask is for you to step out every day and look at the moon.
I figured this season, during this month, the weather would be quite good in most places across the world.
So this is a good time to do it.
Of course in our rush times we have forgotten about nature.
We don't really realize that the very important things by time for example are actually based
on units which are based on the cycles of things happening in the sky.
What is like the moon and the sun are quite important in our lives.
They were well known to our ancestors who had given fantastic mythologies and lovely names
to all of these.
Today of course we know them by the simple scientific names mostly but all of you realize
that they are part of our tradition.
The moon for example is known by so many lovely names.
Selim, Bulan, Chandra, Changi, so many names that it has across the world.
However, how many of us can actually claim that we know the moon as good as our ancestors?
In our whole connected learning of these days, we have kind of stopped individually relating
to information about nature.
Simple things like the moon, the sun, the movements across the sky may not be so well known to us.
Well I'm not complaining.
I'm just saying let us use this time that we have to look at it.
It is a lovely simple activity and I'm actually going to do it with my immediate family.
We are going to look for the moon of course every day but I plan to also observe a bit.
This is going a bit more than looking, simply looking.
In the observations I would probably try to look at what time am I looking at the moon?
Right.

Is it in the west?
Is it at the east?

Maybe just check.
I'm going to look at what is this distance from the horizon.

What is it's rising time?
What did I see it rising?
Did I see it setting?
What are the times of these?
Maybe I'll even make a table out of this.
Just to note down these things every day throughout the whole month.
I might even try to look at it through a binocular or my small telescope.
I'm sure this will be fun and it will be fun activity to do every day for a little bit
of time.
If you do happen to have binoculars or telescopes, why not consider sketching the moon?
See this lovely sketch is by Galileo.
Yes, the first man to look through a telescope towards the moon.
And he could make these sketches.
So why not you?
And I'm sure you'll have a lot of fun doing this.
Of course, if you're not satisfied with these, you could go for photography.
You see this lovely collection of some of the phases of the moon.
Maybe you could try to do all of them and collect all the moon pictures together to form
your own moon calendar.
And this is an animation that you could also go for.
Or the pains this person must have gone through to put together this lovely way of the moon
changing.
So starting this new moon, our friends are going to record a lot of pictures which we would
love to share with you.
We would do a detailed analysis of these pictures, look through all of them and see what are
the beautiful features on the moon that we can spot.
If you yourself miss looking at the moon any of these pictures, don't worry, you can

So don't forget to subscribe to this to get your updates.
We will of course always be giving you nice tidbits like this to add into the fun.
So be with us for the moon challenge all through this month.
I'm sure you will enjoy it so much that you will do it for one more month and then one
